title: Machine Learning Model for Atomic-Level Dynamic Analysis of in situ Environmental Transmission Electron Microscopy Data on Cu2O Embedded in Cu
content: In situ environmental transmission electron microscopy (ETEM) provides atomic-scale insights into the dynamic structural evolution of materials under reaction conditions. However, quantitative analysis of such data is challenging due to the complexity and volume of the data. Previous methods [1,2] for segmenting atomic positions have focused on isolated samples, such as stand-alone nanoparticles or bulk sample. These approaches, however, struggle to differentiate supported samples, such as nanoparticles grown on a crystalline substrate. In this work, using in situ ETEM data on Cu2O reduction under methanol vapor as a case study, we developed a machine learning (ML) model to segment and identify the atomic positions of Cu2O from the Cu substrate, that is robust to conditions such as varying orientations, magnifications, and noise.
